title: Building a Multi-Service Application
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and key terms of building a multi-service application.
Choose and interpret a suitable Docker example connected to building a multi-service application.
Predict an expected result and verify it using observable evidence in a controlled environment.

content.intro: This lesson covers Building a Multi-Service Application. You will connect the named subtopics from the supplied Docker curriculum to a small, observable example. Work through the visual first, then use the example to form a prediction and check it against the actual behavior.
content.why_it_matters: Compose stores the intended shape of an application stack in a declarative YAML file. Inspect the resolved configuration and service health rather than assuming a successful start means the whole application is ready. Learning building a multi-service application helps you make deployment behavior explicit and repeatable instead of relying on a command that happened to work on one machine.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: Start with the supplied example for building a multi-service application. Before running it, state what you expect to happen. Compare the real output with that prediction, then change one variable or setting in a disposable lab to test the boundary of the idea. If a command is not supported on your operating system or installed Docker version, consult the linked official reference and record the actual version rather than guessing.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Building a Multi-Service Application
content_blocks.code:
services:
  web:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:80"
    restart: unless-stopped
content_blocks.expected_output: Compose resolves one web service and maps the container port 80 to loopback port 8080 on the host.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet as compose.yaml, then run `docker compose config` and `docker compose up -d` from that directory.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Stop and remove this lab with `docker compose down`. This is a learning example, not a complete production configuration.
content_blocks.safety_note: Run only against a local test Docker environment. Docker commands are not executed by the CodeLeaf lesson page.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming that a successful start means the application is ready.
common_mistakes.why: A container can start while its dependent service is unavailable or the application is failing after startup.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect health/status and logs; add a meaningful health check or retry strategy where appropriate.

common_mistakes.problem: Keeping required data only in the container writable layer.
common_mistakes.why: Replacing the container can discard that layer and its application state.
common_mistakes.fix: Select a named volume or an external storage system, then rehearse a restore.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a command without checking context, target, or permissions.
common_mistakes.why: Docker commands affect the active endpoint and can change host resources or publish services.
common_mistakes.fix: Check `docker context show`, use an isolated lab, make the smallest change, and verify the resulting state.
